rationale: B wins because it makes the cleaner editorial call: it refuses the no-customer story while A keeps “The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes,” which invents both the delay and the cure. B’s “Wise says stablecoin rails are cheaper — the open question is who keeps the savings” is a real investor beat built from the supplied facts: public, profitable, cheaper rail, mission language. A has sharper reporter targeting and proof lists, but its discipline breaks exactly where it needed to hold.
gaps_in_A: “The businesses waiting three days for a payment that clears in minutes” invents both the old settlement time and the new one. The update only says faster and cheaper; no three-day baseline, no minutes claim, no customer.

“A profitable listed payments company is putting stablecoins on its balance-sheet flows” overstates the facts. The update says businesses can hold and settle in a regulated stablecoin; it does not say Wise is holding stablecoins on its own balance sheet.
The customer angle admits its own fatal flaw: “Without a named customer this angle does not exist” — then it keeps the angle anyway. That is not rigor; that is a warning label on an empty box.

“none of these angles has a current news signal under it” is too cute. The supplied update is a launch with a timestamp; use newsjack-detector for a stronger external peg, not because the launch has no peg.
gaps_in_B: “crossing into regulated, mainstream B2B money movement” is directionally plausible but still a reach. Wise’s scale supports significance; the update gives no live volume, customer count, or adoption proof.
“which bank fees and float revenue get squeezed” leans ahead of the evidence. The update supports a question about incumbent pressure, not an implied revenue hit.

It under-specifies the listed-company risk proof. For public-company and equities angles, it should ask who holds the balances, what custody arrangement applies, what happens on issuer failure, and whether disclosure treatment changes.
The first angle’s “payments or fintech trade reporter” is broader than it needs to be. The rest of the set knows how to name a beat; that one still has a little spray-and-pray left in it.
